subject: MAP: POC orchestration + network checklist (API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@helixhealth.com>, IT Ops <it-ops@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: POC orchestration + network checklist (API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Hi Alicia —

Following our demo, attached is a lightweight mutual action plan (MAP) and a network checklist so we can get a staging POC live. My ask: can you review the milestones below and confirm owners/timelines for Helix so we can lock the MAP and hit a staging cutover target.

High-level milestones (proposed):
- Day 0 (today): Exchange basic network and account info — VPC IDs, CIDRs, peering contact.
- Day 2–5: Create Helix read-only test service account + supply VPC peering details.
- Day 5–10: Redwood provisions org & test API keys, run smoke test, IP allowlist verification.
- Day 10–14: VPC peering validation, performance sanity checks, security evidence review.
- Day 14–21: Staging sign-off and plan for production rollout.

Specific asks we need from Helix to finalize the MAP:
1) Target staging cutover date (suggested: 2026-05-21)
2) Helix VPC ID(s) and owner contact for peering swap
3) Static egress IP ranges to allowlist on your firewall (if you prefer we can provide the IP ranges after we bind the peering)
4) Any org-level constraints (KMS/HSM must be used, IP allowlist windows, restricted ports)
5) Point of contact for procurement/PO and security questionnaire owner

Attachments in this message: Helix-MAP-draft.xlsx (MAP template), redwood-network-reqs.pdf (network checklist and recommended ports).

If you confirm owners and the suggested cutover, we’ll create a short mutual timeline and schedule a 30-min technical runbook call.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@helixhealth.com>

Tessa —

Thanks for the clear plan. We reviewed internally and can move forward with the proposed flow. Quick responses inline:

- Target staging cutover: aiming for 2026-05-21 as you suggested.
- VPC details: primary VPC ID: vpc-0a1b2c3d (us-west-2), owner: Maria Delgado (networks).
- Preliminary IP allowlist for quick tests (these are our public egress ranges): 52.24.12.0/22, 34.213.45.0/24
- Security: our InfoSec needs SOC2 Type II evidence and a short network diagram.
- Procurement: PO process is internal; expect a PO by end of May once POC completes.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: POC orchestration + network checklist (API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Alicia / team —

Great — quick technical notes to make the onboarding smooth:

1) API keys/org setup
- Please create an org-level project and share the org_id (we'll use this to bind API keys to your account).
- For the POC we will issue a time-limited staging API key: header name X-Redwood-Test-Key, value will be provided via a secure link once you confirm org_id.
- If you plan to use KMS/HSM for token encryption, flag that now; we have integrations but need the KMS ARN ahead of time.

2) IP allowlist & peering
- Redwood will initiate a VPC peering request from our VPC (vpc-rw-prod-1). For peering we need your VPC ID, region, and the exact CIDR(s).
- If you prefer not to peer, IP allowlist on Helix firewall for our public egress is sufficient for initial test traffic. Our usual test egress ranges for this environment: 18.205.0.0/16, 3.211.0.0/16.
- No special inbound ports beyond 443 are required for basic inference calls. If you plan to run a private peering route for metrics/tracing, we can open a small set of ports (TCP 50051 for gRPC tracing, optional).

3) Routing/overlap check
- Please confirm there is no CIDR overlap between your VPC and 10.0.0.0/8 (we prefer to avoid overlapping RFC1918 ranges). If overlap exists we can propose a NAT/proxy workaround but it adds 2–3 days.

4) Peering operational contact
- Please send the peering owner contact and a runbook point-of-contact (email + Slack if available).

I attached a small peering-template.txt with route table checklist and required fields for a successful peering. Once we have org_id and peering contact I’ll trigger the staging key issuance.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: peering-template.txt

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Alicia / team —

Quick note from Security/CS: we will run a light security review and a short latency run during the staging window. Proposed internal checkpoints:
- 2026-05-18: security evidence due (SOC2 links, network diagram)
- 2026-05-20: canary test window (30–60 minutes)
- 2026-05-21: staging cutover / smoke sign-off

Can you confirm the expected RPS for the canary and any SLA targets we should validate (p95 latency target)? If you don't have an RPS target, we'll run at a low, medium, and burst profile to capture tail behaviors.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
